thread:
josh_support: Hey team, customer #2456 sending streaming responses in structured_output mode. They say the stream stops mid-JSON and their parser throws `unexpected EOF`. Happens only on SSE/streaming path, non-streaming responses are fine. Stack trace from customer attached.
kevin_eng: Can you paste a minimal repro or curl? Also which model and runtime (hosted/dedicated/private)?
josh_support: Hosted API. Repro curl they provided (sanitized):
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1-stream","mode":"structured_output","prompt":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses/stream
```
Response stream shows two JSON objects but second ends abruptly like:
```
data: {"id":"r1","output":{"items":[{"type":"text","text":"{
  \"user_id\": \"123\",\n  \"profile\": {\"name\": \"Alicia\", \"emails\": [\"al@ex.com\"]}\n"
}
```
(notice trailing open braces). Customer sees parse error in their JS client.
maria_sre: Any intermediate proxies or LB? Also what are tail logs from runtime (stream close events)?
josh_support: Customer is behind an internal corporate proxy + Cloudflare in front of our edge. They can repro without our SDK using raw curl though.
kevin_eng: Two likely failure modes: 1) upstream/network cut (connection reset) truncates the stream mid-chunk, 2) our SSE framing emitted partial JSON because of chunk boundary flush. Need logs: connection close reason, last bytes sent, and whether we emitted end-of-stream event. Can you pull the runtime request_id and last bytes for that session?
ingest-bot: runtime:session=rs-8b2c, model=rwd-1-stream, bytes_sent=16384, closed_by=peer, close_code=RST_STREAM
maria_sre: ingest-bot shows `closed_by=peer` and RST_STREAM. That suggests the client side or intermediate proxy closed the TCP/TLS stream. Cloudflare/Corp proxy might have an idle or max duration limit. Ask customer if they see any corporate proxy logs.
josh_support: Customer gave a tcpdump excerpt showing a FIN from their proxy right after a chunk boundary. They also said when they increase keepalive intervals the issue happened less often.
kevin_eng: Repro plan:
- Have customer run `curl --http2 -N` with `-H "Connection: keep-alive"` and `--no-buffer` to mimic streaming.
- Meanwhile we will tail runtime logs for rs-8b2c and capture last 1s of bytes emitted. Also enable `sse-frame-debug=true` on a debug route to log chunk boundaries (temp).
- Ask SRE to check any ALB/NLB/edge idle timeouts and Cloudflare stream limits.
maria_sre: Also run a minimal local repro that simulates mid-stream RST: python server that sends a few JSONs then resets socket. If our client lib/edge code doesn't emit a final `data: [DONE]` when peer RSTs, downstream parsers will see truncated JSON. We should harden: when we detect RST_CLIENT, append a small `partial_truncation` log and mark the response as truncated in observability so support can surface to customers.
kevin_eng: Agreed. Short-term mitigation for customer: recommend switching to single-shot mode or add a small checkpointing wrapper on their side to tolerate truncated JSON (e.g., stream by line-delimited JSON or use chunked record separators). Long-term we'll add server-side stronger SSE termination and a best-effort partial fragment header so clients can detect truncation.
josh_support: Customer agreed to try keepalive tweaks and run curl test. They've provided additional runtime id: rs-8b2c-2 for a fresh attempt tomorrow.
kevin_eng: I'll open RFC/issue and assign to eng-runtime. Action items:
- kevin_eng: create jira INF-3124 with logs + ingest-bot evidence
- maria_sre: check Cloudflare/edge timeout config and correlate with rs-8b2c timestamps
- josh_support: request tcpdump and curl --http2 -N output from customer for rs-8b2c-2
- eng-runtime: add optional debug logging for SSE chunk boundaries

josh_support: marking P2 for now. Will update once customer runs tests. :thumbsup:
